ledger.note: 8 April 1838: Jhalawar is created from Kota. "it was resolved in the year 1838, with the grudging consent of the chief of Kota, to dismember the state" (infobox Established: 1838; the table begins Madan Singh on 8 April 1838); "by treaty, the new royal family acknowledged the suzerainty of the British" with an annual tribute of £8,000. The parganas are not named; the 1881 area is used for the circle.

region.text: the Jhalawar districts returned to Kota in 1897-1899

ledger.note: 1897-1899: most of Jhalawar goes back to Kota. "the British resolved in 1897 to break up the state, restoring the greater part to Kota, but forming the two districts of Shahabad and the Chaumahla into a new state of area 810 square miles (2,100 km2), which came into existence in 1899". Zalim Singh II had been deposed in 1896. The year is 1899 (the new state's year); the parganas are not named and the annulus is my reading.

sources.title: Jhalawar State
sources.note: Established 1838 by dismembering Kota; Madan Singh, grandson of Zalim Singh, 8 April 1838; tribute of 8,000 pounds; Zalim Singh II deposed 1896; state broken up 1897-1899 with most returned to Kota; area 6,977.5 km2 (1881) and 2,106 km2 (1901).

sources.title: Kota State
sources.note: Kota lost the Jhalawar districts in 1838; British suzerainty over Kota from 1817.

notes: Two pages opened (Jhalawar State, Kota State). The page gives no end date and no merger into Rajasthan, and it does not name the parganas severed from Kota in 1838 or returned in 1899; "Shahabad and Chaumahla became a new state in 1899" is read as the remnant of Jhalawar (2,106 km2 in 1901), which is a reading: the page does not say that the new state is the continuation of Jhalawar. The 1881 area (6,977.5 km2) and the 1901 area (2,106 km2) are both given for Jhalawar. Zalim Singh, the regent of Kota from 1771, is the grandfather of Madan Singh; the page does not date the end of his regency. british-empire (sa-06) should record the vassal_start for jhalawar-state from 1838 (the treaty acknowledged British suzerainty) to 1947. kota-state has a dossier in this batch.
